article.title: ICBL: North Korea’s reported mine-laying could be world’s largest since 2001
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Korean article.

South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff told members of the National Assembly’s intelligence and defense committee last month that North Korea has laid an estimated 960,000 land mines in the Demilitarized Zone since 2024.
South Korean media, citing lawmakers’ offices, reported that the military had presented the estimate to the National Assembly in late October.
VOA reached out to the International Campaign to Ban Landmines for a response to the news, but the ICBL said it could not independently verify the figure or explain how it was calculated.
The ICBL did tell VOA that if the 960-thousand mine figure is accurate, it would be one of the "largest uses of antipersonnel mines anywhere in the world..."
But it's not the largest. In Russia’s war in Ukraine, international experts estimate Russia has laid more than 2 million land mines since 2022, according to the U.S. State Department.
The ICBL did say that North Korean landmines can float into waterways beyond the Demilitarized Zone, threatening civilians and soldiers with injuries likely to cost them a limb.
The ICBL notably shared the 1997 Nobel Peace Prize with Jody Williams for efforts to ban and clear antipersonnel mines.

Separately, South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff concluded on October 5 that North Korean antipersonnel mines deliberately planted on the South Korean-controlled side of the DMZ caused the September 21 explosions that injured three South Korean troops.
Citing a joint investigation with United Nations Command and forensic testing, the military said those mines had been planted rather than washed into the area.

North Korea rejected responsibility for planting the mines. In an October 25 letter to the U.N. Security Council president, Pyongyang called the incident a South Korean fabrication intended to obstruct its border fortifications and evade blame for worsening tensions.
zh: ICBL：據報導，北韓此次布雷行動可能是自2001年以來規模最大的一次
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）的韓文原文報導。
南韓參謀總長上個月向國會情報與國防委員會委員表示，自2024年以來，北韓已在非軍事區埋設了約96萬枚地雷。
南韓媒體援引國會議員辦公室的消息報導，軍方已於10月下旬向國會提交了這份預算估算。
美國之音（VOA）就這則新聞聯繫了「國際禁用地雷運動」（ICBL）尋求回應，但該組織表示無法獨立核實該數據，也無法說明其計算方式。
國際禁雷運動組織（ICBL）確實向美國之音表示，如果96萬枚地雷的數字屬實，這將是「全球範圍內最大規模的殺傷人員地雷使用案例之一……」
但這並非規模最大的。根據美國國務院的資料，在俄羅斯對烏克蘭的戰爭中，國際專家估計，自2022年以來，俄羅斯已埋設超過200萬枚地雷。
國際禁雷運動（ICBL）確實指出，北韓的地雷可能會漂流至非軍事區以外的水域，對平民和士兵構成威脅，導致他們受傷甚至可能喪失肢體。
國際禁雷運動組織（ICBL）因致力於禁止及清除殺傷人員地雷，而與喬迪·威廉斯共同榮獲1997年諾貝爾和平獎，這一點尤為值得注意。
此外，南韓聯合參謀本部於10月5日認定，北韓在非軍事區（DMZ）南韓控制一側蓄意埋設的殺傷人員地雷，是導致9月21日爆炸事件的肇因，該事件造成三名南韓軍人受傷。
軍方援引與聯合國司令部進行的聯合調查及法醫鑑定結果指出，這些地雷是被人埋設的，而非被沖入該區域。
北韓否認埋設地雷的責任。平壤在10月25日致聯合國安全理事會主席的一封信中，稱此事件是南韓捏造的，意在阻撓其邊境防禦工程，並逃避對局勢緊張加劇的責任。
